text:
The Red Wings are 7-7-3, and if you only looked at the standings you'd call them average. The process says more. Detroit has 52% of the expected goals and creates 3.24 per hour, but has scored nine fewer goals than those chances usually produce. Our numbers figure they've left about two and a half points on the table, which is the gap between 17 points and roughly 19.5.

The kids are carrying the bright side. Alex DeBrincat with Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has outscored opponents 8-1 at five on five with 64% of the chances. Swap Viktor Arvidsson in for Brandsegg-Nygård and it's still good (60%). Dylan Larkin's line with Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond has the process (56%) but only one goal for and three against.

The back end is quieter. Ben Chiarot and Moritz Seider have played 201 minutes together at an even 51% and been outscored 9-5. The power play generates 0.83 expected goals a game, a decent rate.

Then there's the noise. The Athletic's Michael Russo reported the Wild are pushing hard for Larkin, framed as a "breakup with Red Wings." That's a story to follow, not one our numbers can settle. On the ice, the fix may simply be time: playoff odds of 32% are the price of a slow start, not a bad team.
headline: Detroit deserves better than .500
